title.en: Hear both sides of a debate
title.es: Escuchar las dos posturas de un debate

es: Reconocer en un debate escolar dónde el hablante concede un punto, dónde lo rebate y dónde concluye.

vocabulary.es: te doy la razón en que, admito que
una norma que se aplica a todos por igual

teaching.en: Admittedly, a phone is a lifeline in an emergency, but the office already has a landline for pupils.
teaching.es: Es cierto que un celular es un salvavidas en una emergencia, pero la oficina ya tiene un teléfono fijo para los alumnos.
teaching.explanationEs: Admittedly abre la concesión; el but posterior abre la refutación, que es lo que el hablante defiende de verdad.
segments: Admittedly, a phone is a lifeline in an emergency,
but the office already has a landline for pupils.
teaching.audioText: Admittedly, a phone is a lifeline in an emergency, but the office already has a landline for pupils.

teaching.en: I concede that an outright ban is easy to explain, but its claim to raise results does not hold water.
teaching.es: Reconozco que una prohibición total es fácil de explicar, pero su pretensión de mejorar los resultados no se sostiene.
teaching.explanationEs: I concede that… cede un punto y but abre lo que se defiende. Hold water = resistir un examen: casi siempre se usa en negativa.
segments: I concede that an outright ban is easy to explain,
but its claim to raise results does not hold water.
teaching.audioText: I concede that an outright ban is easy to explain, but its claim to raise results does not hold water.

teaching.en: That is a valid worry, and I grant you that phones distract from lessons; that said, a blanket rule punishes everyone.
teaching.es: Es una preocupación válida, y te doy la razón en que los celulares distraen de las clases; dicho esto, una norma para todos por igual castiga a todos.
teaching.explanationEs: I grant you that… concede con tono generoso; that said es un giro suave, parecido a «aun así».
segments: That is a valid worry, and I grant you that phones
distract from lessons; that said, a blanket rule punishes everyone.
teaching.audioText: That is a valid worry, and I grant you that phones distract from lessons; that said, a blanket rule punishes everyone.

teaching.en: Some pupils do use their phones sensibly; nevertheless, a single rule for everyone is easier to enforce and harder to dispute.
teaching.es: Algunos alumnos sí usan el celular con sensatez; sin embargo, una sola norma para todos es más fácil de aplicar y más difícil de discutir.
teaching.explanationEs: Nevertheless va detrás del punto concedido (some pupils do…) y abre lo que el hablante prefiere defender.
segments: Some pupils do use their phones sensibly; nevertheless, a single rule
for everyone is easier to enforce and harder to dispute.
teaching.audioText: Some pupils do use their phones sensibly; nevertheless, a single rule for everyone is easier to enforce and harder to dispute.

teaching.en: To conclude, and on balance, I would keep phones in bags during lessons but allow them at break.
teaching.es: Para concluir, y sopesándolo todo, guardaría los celulares en las mochilas durante las clases, pero los permitiría en el recreo.
teaching.explanationEs: To conclude anuncia el cierre; on balance indica que has sopesado los dos lados antes de decidir.
segments: To conclude, and on balance, I would keep phones
in bags during lessons but allow them at break.
teaching.audioText: To conclude, and on balance, I would keep phones in bags during lessons but allow them at break.

teaching.en: A fair-minded speaker will concede the strongest objection first, then take issue with it calmly.
teaching.es: Un orador justo concederá primero la objeción más fuerte y luego discrepará de ella con calma.
teaching.explanationEs: Conceder lo más fuerte del otro lado da credibilidad; take issue with = discrepar de, poner objeciones a.
segments: A fair-minded speaker will concede the strongest objection
first, then take issue with it calmly.
teaching.audioText: A fair-minded speaker will concede the strongest objection first, then take issue with it calmly.

prompt.es: Localiza la concesión: ¿qué reconoce la hablante antes de girar?

choices.text: That a ringing phone can pull attention away from a lesson.
That a locker system deserves a one-term trial in this school.
That phones ruin concentration in every lesson, as some teachers claim.

feedback.es: La concesión llega antes de «That said»: admite que una pantalla que vibra distrae; el ensayo con taquillas es lo que propone ella y arruinar la concentración es lo que alegan otros.

hint.es: La concesión es lo que admite antes del giro, no lo que defiende después.

origin.text: Some teachers argue that phones ruin concentration, and I grant you that a ringing phone can distract from a lesson. That said, our school has never tried a simple locker system, so nobody can claim it failed. On balance, I would like to see it tested for one term.

prompt.es: Completa: «Te doy la razón: puede serlo, pero la oficina tiene un teléfono gratuito.»

answer.text: grant

feedback.es: I grant you that… es la fórmula de concesión generosa; concede no admite «you» detrás.

hint.es: Verbo que significa «admitir, dar la razón»; empieza por g.

origin.text: Some pupils say a phone is a lifeline after dark. I ___ you that it can be, but the office phone is free to use.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Es un punto válido, pero la norma sigue en pie.»

answer.text: That is a valid point but the rule still stands

feedback.es: La concesión (valid point) va primero y el giro con but introduce lo que se defiende.

hint.es: Primero la concesión, después but y tu postura.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué concede la hablante sobre las clases con celular.

choices.text: That a dictionary check is a poor reason to allow phones.
That some pupils do waste whole lessons staring at their own screens.
That a traffic-light system would be unfair to teachers.

feedback.es: «I accept that some pupils stare at their screens…» es la concesión; «Even so» abre la refutación y el semáforo es su propuesta.

origin.audio: Ms Reyes says phones should stay in bags all day. I see where she is coming from, and I accept that some pupils stare at their screens for an entire lesson. Even so, a blanket rule punishes those who use a phone to check a dictionary. She could try a traffic-light system instead, with green for research and red for silence.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase del debate con la función que cumple.

pairs: Admittedly, the rule is easy to explain
That said, it is hard to enforce
On balance, I would keep it
That argument does not hold water
One phone rang during the test

feedback.es: Cada marcador cumple un papel: Admittedly concede, that said gira, on balance cierra, hold water descarta y one phone rang ilustra.

pairs: Admittedly, the rule is easy to explain
That said, it is hard to enforce
On balance, I would keep it
That argument does not hold water
One phone rang during the test

prompt.es: ¿Qué defiende realmente Tom en este resumen de su intervención?

choices.text: That phones in emergencies are so important that no rule should limit them.
That pupils who use phones sensibly should be punished along with the rest.
That the ban is reasonable because pupils can already phone home from school.

feedback.es: Tom concede el valor del celular en una emergencia, pero lo que defiende es que la prohibición es razonable porque ya existe otra vía.

origin.text: Tom's speech opened with a concession: phones do let pupils reach home in an emergency. He then turned sharply, pointing out that the same pupils already have access to the school office. His closing line was more cautious, suggesting only that the ban should be reviewed after one term.

prompt.es: Escucha el fragmento y elige qué concede Leo antes de su giro.

choices.text: That a newcomer might depend on a translation app.
That most pupils use translation apps to cheat in tests.
That Mia had used a translation app herself at school.
That Mia's point deserved more attention than it had received.

feedback.es: La concesión es la generosidad inicial hacia el punto de Mia: un alumno recién llegado puede depender de la aplicación; lo demás es una generalización, un dato no mencionado o una opinión que Leo no expresa.

origin.audio: At Tuesday's debate, Leo argued for keeping phones in bags. He opened generously: Mia's point about translation apps was fair, he said, and he could see how a pupil new to the country might rely on one. Even so, he went on, the same app can write a whole essay in seconds, and teachers cannot tell the difference from across the room. He did not claim that every pupil cheats; he said only that a rule has to work for the pupils who do. On balance, he thought a ban in tests and a free hand in practice lessons was the honest middle ground, although he admitted the school might struggle to enforce it.

prompt.es: Escucha de nuevo: ¿qué actitud muestra Leo hacia su propia propuesta final?

choices.text: He presents it as a perfect answer that leaves nothing more to discuss.
He offers a fair compromise but admits it may be hard to apply.
He proposes it reluctantly and would drop it the moment teachers object.
He sees it as a fair compromise that most teachers will gladly welcome.

feedback.es: Leo llama «honest middle ground» a su propuesta, pero admite que aplicarla puede costar: actitud de compromiso realista, no de certeza ni de desgana.

origin.audio: At Tuesday's debate, Leo argued for keeping phones in bags. He opened generously: Mia's point about translation apps was fair, he said, and he could see how a pupil new to the country might rely on one. Even so, he went on, the same app can write a whole essay in seconds, and teachers cannot tell the difference from across the room. He did not claim that every pupil cheats; he said only that a rule has to work for the pupils who do. On balance, he thought a ban in tests and a free hand in practice lessons was the honest middle ground, although he admitted the school might struggle to enforce it.

prompt.es: Completa: «La directora estaba dispuesta a conceder que la norma era confusa.»

answer.text: concede

feedback.es: Concede that… es la colocación natural para reconocer un punto ajeno sin cambiar la postura; los sinónimos admit o accept también encajan.

origin.text: The head teacher was prepared to ___ that the old rule had been unclear. She would not, however, drop it completely, and she asked the council to give it one more term.

prompt.es: Escribe una concesión y una refutación sobre traductores en exámenes.

answer.text: I grant you that a translation app can help newcomers; that said, in a test it would be unfair to pupils who have learned the words.
accepted: I grant you that a translation app can help newcomers; that said, in a test it would be unfair to pupils who have learned the words.
Admittedly, a translation app helps pupils who are new to the country; nevertheless, in an exam it would be unfair to those who have studied the words.
I concede that an app can help newcomers, but in a test it would be unfair to pupils who have learned the vocabulary.

feedback.es: Una buena respuesta concede con una fórmula (I grant you, admittedly, I concede) y gira después hacia la postura propia.

origin.text: Concede que un traductor ayuda a los alumnos recién llegados y rebate que en un examen sería injusto para quienes han estudiado las palabras.

prompt.es: ¿Con qué propósito escribe Sara este correo a la dirección?

choices.text: To drop the council's objection now that she understands the rule.
To accuse the staff of ignoring what the survey of pupils clearly shows.
To ask for a delay so that the council's findings can be considered.
To propose that the ban apply at break but not in lessons, as pupils prefer.

feedback.es: Sara reconoce la postura del centro, pero su petición es esperar a los resultados completos: busca aplazar, no retirar ni acusar.

origin.text: Dear Head Teacher, thank you for meeting the pupil council. I understand why you want a single rule, and I do not doubt that staff are under pressure. All the same, our survey suggests that most pupils would accept a ban in lessons but not at break. I would therefore ask you to hold off on the outright ban until we have shared the full results next week.

prompt.es: Ordena: «En conjunto, el argumento a favor de la prohibición no se sostiene.»

answer.text: On balance the case for a ban does not hold water
accepted: On balance the case for a ban does not hold water
The case for a ban does not hold water on balance

feedback.es: On balance abre una valoración global y does not hold water descarta el argumento.

prompt.es: Completa: «La última razón, francamente, no se sostenía.»

answer.text: water

feedback.es: Hold water (o hold up) describe un argumento que resiste el examen; Carlos debió conceder que el cuarto no lo hacía.

origin.text: Carlos listed four reasons for the ban. The first three were strong; the last one, frankly, did not hold ___. He should have conceded as much.

title.en: Much as I admire the plan
title.es: Por mucho que admire el plan

es: Formar concesivas avanzadas con much as, however + adjetivo y adjetivo + as/though en lugar de although.

vocabulary.es: a pesar de que, pese a lo mucho que

teaching.en: Much as I admire the council's ambition, I cannot back a scheme that comes with a hefty fee.
teaching.es: Por mucho que admire la ambición del municipio, no puedo respaldar un plan que trae consigo una cuota abultada.
teaching.explanationEs: Much as + sujeto + verbo = «por mucho que»; el verbo va en indicativo y la postura sigue sin but.
segments: Much as I admire the council's ambition, I cannot
back a scheme that comes with a hefty fee.
teaching.audioText: Much as I admire the council's ambition, I cannot back a scheme that comes with a hefty fee.

teaching.en: However tempting the free trial may be, nobody should be swayed by it before reading the small print.
teaching.es: Por muy tentadora que sea la prueba gratuita, nadie debería dejarse influir por ella antes de leer la letra pequeña.
teaching.explanationEs: However + adjetivo + sujeto + verbo; may be añade posibilidad («por muy tentadora que pueda ser»).
segments: However tempting the free trial may be, nobody should
be swayed by it before reading the small print.
teaching.audioText: However tempting the free trial may be, nobody should be swayed by it before reading the small print.

teaching.en: Strict though the new rules may seem, they have one clear advantage: nobody can claim they were applied unfairly.
teaching.es: Por estrictas que parezcan las nuevas normas, tienen una ventaja clara: nadie puede alegar que se aplicaron injustamente.
teaching.explanationEs: Adjetivo + though + sujeto + verbo: el adjetivo pasa al principio; puedes cambiar though por as.
segments: Strict though the new rules may seem, they have one
clear advantage: nobody can claim they were applied unfairly.
teaching.audioText: Strict though the new rules may seem, they have one clear advantage: nobody can claim they were applied unfairly.

teaching.en: Clever as the proposal is, it has a fatal flaw: it depends on every household paying on time.
teaching.es: Por ingeniosa que sea la propuesta, tiene un defecto fatal: depende de que todos los hogares paguen a tiempo.
teaching.explanationEs: Con as el adjetivo también va delante, y la segunda parte no lleva but.
segments: Clever as the proposal is, it has a fatal
flaw: it depends on every household paying on time.
teaching.audioText: Clever as the proposal is, it has a fatal flaw: it depends on every household paying on time.

teaching.en: However much effort the staff put in, the plan will come at a cost that somebody must pay.
teaching.es: Por mucho esfuerzo que haga el personal, el plan tendrá un precio que alguien deberá pagar.
teaching.explanationEs: However much + nombre + sujeto + verbo = «por mucho… que»; come at a cost significa tener un precio, salir caro.
segments: However much effort the staff put in, the plan
will come at a cost that somebody must pay.
teaching.audioText: However much effort the staff put in, the plan will come at a cost that somebody must pay.

teaching.en: Tempting as the trip was, Mia turned it down; for all that she admired the organisers, the fee was too steep.
teaching.es: Aunque el viaje era tentador, Mia lo rechazó; pese a lo mucho que admiraba a los organizadores, la cuota era excesiva.
teaching.explanationEs: For all that + sujeto + verbo = «a pesar de que», con tono formal; en pasado la estructura funciona igual.
segments: Tempting as the trip was, Mia turned it down; for all
that she admired the organisers, the fee was too steep.
teaching.audioText: Tempting as the trip was, Mia turned it down; for all that she admired the organisers, the fee was too steep.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Por mucho que valoremos la biblioteca, no podemos pagar la cuota.»

answer.text: Much as we value the library we cannot pay the fee
accepted: Much as we value the library we cannot pay the fee
We cannot pay the fee much as we value the library

feedback.es: Much as + sujeto + verbo abre la concesión y la postura sigue sin but; el orden inverso también es natural.

hint.es: Empieza por Much as y no añadas but.

prompt.es: Completa: «Por pequeña que suene, sigue siendo una subida del veinte por ciento.»

answer.text: However

feedback.es: Tras However va el adjetivo, luego el sujeto y el verbo: However small it may sound equivale a «por pequeña que suene».

hint.es: Va delante del adjetivo y significa «por muy… que».

origin.text: The bus company calls the new fare a small adjustment. ___ small it may sound, it is still a rise of twenty per cent for people on low incomes.

prompt.es: Elige la frase bien formada con adjetivo + though.

choices.text: Generous though sounds the offer, it comes at a cost.
Generous though the offer sounds, it comes at a cost.
Though generous the offer sounds, but it comes at a cost.

feedback.es: El adjetivo abre la frase y le siguen though, el sujeto y el verbo, sin invertir el orden ni añadir but.

hint.es: Tras though viene el sujeto y luego el verbo; la segunda parte no lleva but.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige la actitud de la hablante hacia el plan de la biblioteca.

choices.text: Content with the plan, since she expects the council to cover the repairs.
On the side of the architects, who she feels have been unfairly blamed for the cost.
Admiring of the library, yet worried about who will meet the repair bills.

feedback.es: La hablante concede la admiración con «Much as…», pero lo que destaca es la preocupación por el coste y por quién pagará las reparaciones; ni confía en que el municipio pague ni defiende a los arquitectos.

origin.audio: Much as the residents admire the new library, they cannot ignore what it will cost them. However popular the plan is, it will raise their bills by eight per cent. Generous though the architects have been, and for all that the building is lovely, nobody has explained who will pay for the repairs.

prompt.es: Completa: «Por mucho dinero que recaude, el techo no se reparará antes del invierno.»

answer.text: much

feedback.es: However much + nombre no contable (money) equivale a «por mucho dinero que»; con nombres contables usarías however many.

origin.text: The club has worked hard all year. However ___ money it raises, the roof will not be repaired before winter.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Por ingenioso que sea el plan, tendrá un precio.»

answer.text: However clever the plan is it will come at a cost
accepted: However clever the plan is it will come at a cost
It will come at a cost however clever the plan is

feedback.es: However clever va pegado delante del sujeto the plan; después el verbo is cierra la concesión.

prompt.es: Escucha la noticia y elige por qué la líder rechaza conservar la piscina vieja.

choices.text: Repairing the old building would cost far more than replacing it.
The volunteers had stopped looking after the old building.
The council had already promised money for a new pool elsewhere.
The pool had been losing money for several years already.

feedback.es: La líder lo dice con «however much effort…»: los arreglos costarían más que una piscina nueva; el resto reinterpreta datos que no aparecen o que ella contradice.

origin.audio: At last night's meeting about the swimming pool, the council leader spoke first. Much as she admired the volunteers who had kept the old building open, she said, the roof was beyond repair, and however much effort they put in, the repairs would cost more than a new pool. Tempting as it was to keep the old one for sentimental reasons, she could not recommend it. A resident then rose to answer. Small though the pool was, he said, it was the only one within ten miles, and for all that the figures looked convincing, nobody had asked the families who use it. The leader thanked him, promised nothing, and closed the meeting.

prompt.es: Escucha de nuevo: ¿qué sugiere el final de la noticia sobre la decisión de la líder?

choices.text: She has been persuaded and will now reopen the old pool.
She has heard his point without committing to change her plan.
She is annoyed by his remarks and rejects everything he said.
She will ask the families who use the pool before voting.

feedback.es: La líder le da las gracias pero «promised nothing»: reconoce el argumento sin comprometerse a cambiar de plan; no dice que consultará ni que se haya convencido.

origin.audio: At last night's meeting about the swimming pool, the council leader spoke first. Much as she admired the volunteers who had kept the old building open, she said, the roof was beyond repair, and however much effort they put in, the repairs would cost more than a new pool. Tempting as it was to keep the old one for sentimental reasons, she could not recommend it. A resident then rose to answer. Small though the pool was, he said, it was the only one within ten miles, and for all that the figures looked convincing, nobody had asked the families who use it. The leader thanked him, promised nothing, and closed the meeting.

prompt.es: Completa: «Mia se negó a dejarse influir por la prueba gratuita y leyó la letra pequeña.»

answer.text: swayed

feedback.es: Be swayed by es la colocación para dejarse influir por algo; tempted o persuaded también son posibles en este contexto.

origin.text: Mia refused to be ___ by the free trial. It looked generous, but she read the small print before she signed anything.

prompt.es: Reescribe con Much as en lugar de Although.

answer.text: Much as I admire the ambition, I think the plan will come at a cost that families cannot afford.
accepted: Much as I admire the ambition, I think the plan will come at a cost that families cannot afford.
Much as I admire the ambition I think the plan will come at a cost that families cannot afford.
Much as I admire the ambition, I believe the plan will come at a cost that families cannot afford.

feedback.es: Although + sujeto + verbo pasa a Much as + sujeto + verbo y el resto de la frase se mantiene, sin but.

origin.text: Although I admire the ambition, I think the plan will come at a cost that families cannot afford.

evidenceGroups: much as i admire the ambition
the plan will come at a cost

prompt.es: ¿Qué pretende lograr esta carta de los vecinos al municipio?

choices.text: To reject the proposal as clever in theory but unrealistic in practice.
To praise the committee's goodwill as the real answer to the funding gap.
To obtain a change to the payment terms instead of rejecting the plan.
To persuade residents to vote against any new fee that the council proposes.

feedback.es: Los vecinos reconocen el ingenio del plan, señalan el defecto y piden repartir el pago: buscan cambiar las condiciones, no rechazarlo.

origin.text: Dear councillors, clever as the proposal is, it has a flaw that we cannot overlook. It assumes that every household can pay the new fee in a single payment, and however much goodwill there is on the committee, goodwill will not cover the gap for families on low incomes. We therefore ask the council to spread the payment over twelve months before any vote is taken.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Aunque admiraba el plan, votó en contra.»

answer.text: For all that she admired the plan she voted against it
accepted: For all that she admired the plan she voted against it
She voted against it for all that she admired the plan

feedback.es: For all that + sujeto + verbo equivale a «a pesar de que» y abre la concesión antes de la decisión.

prompt.es: Completa: «La subida de este año es considerable: casi el doble del precio anterior.»

answer.text: hefty

feedback.es: Hefty es el adjetivo habitual para una cuota o subida grande; steep o substantial también encajan aquí.

origin.text: Families have paid the membership fee for years without complaint. This year's rise, however, is a ___ one: nearly double the old price.

title.en: Follow the argument line by line
title.es: Seguir el hilo de un argumento

es: Distinguir tesis, evidencia, objeción y réplica en un debate escuchado y ordenarlas en un esquema.

teaching.en: I put forward a claim that traffic should stay out of the centre on Sundays, and our survey can lend weight to it.
teaching.es: Planteo la tesis de que el tráfico debería quedar fuera del centro los domingos, y nuestra encuesta puede darle más peso.
teaching.explanationEs: Put forward a claim = plantear una tesis; lend weight to = reforzar una idea con datos.
segments: I put forward a claim that traffic should stay out of the
centre on Sundays, and our survey can lend weight to it.
teaching.audioText: I put forward a claim that traffic should stay out of the centre on Sundays, and our survey can lend weight to it.

teaching.en: On the face of it, a survey of twenty friends looks like hard evidence; only a representative sample speaks for a town.
teaching.es: A primera vista, una encuesta a veinte amigos parece una prueba sólida; solo una muestra representativa habla por todo un pueblo.
teaching.explanationEs: On the face of it introduce una apariencia que luego se corrige; la evidencia debe ser comprobable y amplia.
segments: On the face of it, a survey of twenty friends looks
like hard evidence; only a representative sample speaks for a town.
teaching.audioText: On the face of it, a survey of twenty friends looks like hard evidence; only a representative sample speaks for a town.

teaching.en: In my opinion the street is nicer without cars, but an opinion on its own is not evidence, however strongly it is held.
teaching.es: En mi opinión la calle es más agradable sin autos, pero una opinión por sí sola no es evidencia, por firmemente que se sostenga.
teaching.explanationEs: La evidencia se puede comprobar; la opinión solo se puede compartir. No las mezcles en tu argumento.
segments: In my opinion the street is nicer without cars, but an opinion
on its own is not evidence, however strongly it is held.
teaching.audioText: In my opinion the street is nicer without cars, but an opinion on its own is not evidence, however strongly it is held.

teaching.en: One shopkeeper may raise an objection: older people cannot walk far; the rebuttal is that a free bus would carry them.
teaching.es: Un comerciante puede plantear una objeción: las personas mayores no pueden caminar lejos; la réplica es que un autobús gratuito las llevaría.
teaching.explanationEs: La objeción es el argumento contrario; la réplica (rebuttal) responde a esa objeción con un dato o una solución.
segments: One shopkeeper may raise an objection: older people cannot walk far;
the rebuttal is that a free bus would carry them.
teaching.audioText: One shopkeeper may raise an objection: older people cannot walk far; the rebuttal is that a free bus would carry them.

teaching.en: Figures that support a claim carry little weight if the source is hidden, because nobody can check where they came from.
teaching.es: Las cifras que respaldan una tesis pesan poco si la fuente está oculta, porque nadie puede comprobar de dónde proceden.
teaching.explanationEs: Support = respaldar. Una cifra sin fuente no se puede verificar, por eso no funciona como evidencia.
segments: Figures that support a claim carry little weight if the source
is hidden, because nobody can check where they came from.
teaching.audioText: Figures that support a claim carry little weight if the source is hidden, because nobody can check where they came from.

teaching.en: Sketch an outline first: your claim, hard evidence, the likeliest objection, and a rebuttal that can cast doubt on it.
teaching.es: Haz primero un esquema: tu tesis, pruebas sólidas, la objeción más probable y una réplica que pueda poner esta en duda.
teaching.explanationEs: Un esquema (outline) ordena las cuatro piezas; cast doubt on = poner en duda, sin necesidad de demostrar lo contrario.
segments: Sketch an outline first: your claim, hard evidence, the likeliest
objection, and a rebuttal that can cast doubt on it.
teaching.audioText: Sketch an outline first: your claim, hard evidence, the likeliest objection, and a rebuttal that can cast doubt on it.

prompt.es: Localiza la evidencia: ¿qué parte de este texto se puede comprobar?

choices.text: The bus system looks out of date and should be replaced soon.
The town needs more routes so that every resident feels part of public life.
A third of residents miss evening events as the last bus leaves early.

es: Rebatir con tacto y firmeza usando atenuantes, refuerzos y frases hendidas en un texto argumentativo.

origin.audio: Carlos got up at the residents' meeting to answer Mia's proposal for a parking charge. He began by conceding that she had a reasonable point: the street really is crowded at weekends. He added that he had reservations about the timing, since a charge introduced in January would hit people who had just paid for the holidays. He never raised his voice. He simply repeated, calmly, that what matters is that nobody is priced out of their own street.

prompt.es: Escribe tu intervención: concesión, refutación con frase hendida y cierre.

answer.text: In my view, pupils should clean their own classroom once a week. Admittedly, it takes time away from lessons, and I have reservations about how often we can do it during exams. That is a reasonable point, but what matters is the habit we build: it is the pupils who use the room every day who should look after it, and it is undoubtedly fairer that everyone shares the work. Arguably, a clean room also helps us study, because nobody concentrates well among rubbish. Far from being a burden, ten minutes on Friday is a small price to pay. It is the cost of extra staff that the school would carry otherwise, and that money could buy books instead. To a large degree, the question is about respect, and what is essential is that we treat the classroom as ours. To conclude, a tidy room by no means needs a cleaner, only a rota.
accepted: In my view, pupils should clean their own classroom once a week. Admittedly, it takes time away from lessons, and I have reservations about how often we can do it during exams. That is a reasonable point, but what matters is the habit we build: it is the pupils who use the room every day who should look after it, and it is undoubtedly fairer that everyone shares the work. Arguably, a clean room also helps us study, because nobody concentrates well among rubbish. Far from being a burden, ten minutes on Friday is a small price to pay. It is the cost of extra staff that the school would carry otherwise, and that money could buy books instead. To a large degree, the question is about respect, and what is essential is that we treat the classroom as ours. To conclude, a tidy room by no means needs a cleaner, only a rota.

I believe that pupils should clean their classroom every week. I concede that it takes time from lessons, and some parents think the school should do it. That is a valid point, but what counts is the habit we learn. It is the pupils who use the room all day, so it is undoubtedly fair that we look after it. Arguably, a clean room helps us study, because nobody concentrates well among rubbish. It is also the cost that the school would save, and that money could buy books for the library. Far from being unfair, ten minutes on Friday is a small price to pay. To a large degree this is a question of respect, and what is essential is that we share the work, because the classroom belongs to all of us. In conclusion, the whole class benefits, and nobody is asked to do more than a fair share.

feedback.es: Una buena intervención concede antes de rebatir, usa al menos una frase hendida, equilibra atenuantes y refuerzos y cierra con una conclusión.
